author: DTrim99
body:
Confirmed — three separate effects here, reconciling our −$841.62 to TaxAct's $562 refund exactly:

| Component | policyengine-taxsim | TaxAct 1040ME |
|---|---|---|
| Maine EIC (Schedule A, line 4) | 0.00 | 325 |
| Property Tax Fairness Credit (25d) | 21.62 | 22 |
| Sales Tax Fairness Credit (25e) | 220.00 | 215 |
| 2025 "affordability payment" (not a return item) | 600.00 | — |
| **Refund** | **841.62** | **562** |

1. **You're right about the EIC.** 36 M.R.S. [§5219-S](https://legislature.maine.gov/statutes/36/title36sec5219-S.html) sub-§6 extends "eligible individual" to childless filers at least 18 but under 25 (sub-§7 adds ITIN filers), and sub-§5 requires the credit to be "calculated in the same manner as it would be calculated if that individual were eligible for a federal earned income credit" — the pro forma computation at the bottom of the worksheet you attached. Pro forma childless federal EIC on $10,476 earned is $649, × 50% (no qualifying child) = $324.50 → TaxAct's $325. PolicyEngine's `me_eitc` currently just multiplies the actual federal EIC by 50%, so it returns 0 for this couple. Filed as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#8927.

2. **STFC:** the [2025 Schedule PTFC/STFC](https://www.maine.gov/revenue/sites/maine.gov.revenue/files/inline-files/25_1040me_sch_ptfc_fillable.pdf#page=4) table gives married-joint / 0 dependents $215 (income ≤ $50,950); PolicyEngine's 2025 base amount is $220. Filed as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#8928.

3. **The remaining $600** is Maine's one-time "affordability payment" (H.P. 1491, Part T): $300 per non-dependent adult, keyed to the 2025 return but mailed by the assessor from a Special Revenue Fund in 2026–27 — never a 1040ME line. PolicyEngine models it as a refundable credit for policy analysis, so it was landing in siitax. #1065 zeroes it in the emulator (same approach as the imputed-transfers fix in #1049); with that change this record returns siitax = −241.62, and it will reconcile to your $562 once the two policyengine-us fixes land.
